transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent mutable `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` argument and naming the return.

Attached the generated split_first_chunk_mut prefix/tail Option and mutable final-frame postcondition directly to the executable target; this records the contract under test and does not assume the target body.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 flow: `let Some((first, tail)) = self.split_at_mut_checked(N) else { return None }; Some((unsafe { &mut *(first.as_mut_ptr().cast_array()) }, tail))`, with only receiver/signature adaptation.

Reused the reviewed split_at_mut_checked relation for the mutable prefix/tail split and final-frame facts, then isolated only the Verus-unsupported first.as_mut_ptr(), ptr.cast_array(), and unsafe mutable array-reference dereference as source-backed local boundaries following the first_chunk_mut mutable cast-array pattern.
